R309 — XeStrata b9 decode-side port candidates for the B570/5600X
Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo)
Status: read-only comparison. No source edits, tests/imports/builds, model/GPU/profiler/process activity, Git operation, or cleanup. I did not inspect the active b9 model/run receipts.

## Finding

The b9-vs-da CPU decode delta contains no new IQ3_S or IQ4_NL row-decoder algorithm and no new Ryzen-5600X default dispatch to recommend for the current Qwen3.8 IQ3_S GU / IQ4_NL Down route. The new AVX2 row kernels are for K-quant and Q8_0 formats; mixed gate/up layout support only matters when the two packed GU tensors have different types. For the stated Qwen pair (type 21 GU, type 20 Down), neither changes the decoder work. The IQ3_S AVX2 route already defaults to NT=1 on AVX2-without-AVX-512 when its environment override is absent, in b9 and the curated tree. Existing IQ3_S gather/prefetch behavior and the previously audited paired-GU experiment are not b9 innovations; the curated source already has an opt-in paired-GU implementation.

One new conditional decode candidate is the b9 fused cache-hit addition plus multi-token MoE combine. It can skip the separate hit-add kernel and intermediate modification of expert output rows when native multi-token combination is explicitly enabled and a verifier window has more than one token. It cannot help the current stated no-MTP, batch-zero, one-token decode route; do not treat it as an immediate B570 throughput candidate or enable it as a generic default.

## Ranked candidate

### 1. Conditional fused hit-add + batched verifier combine (new in b9; not in curated 17879)

In b9 `src/core/verify.cpp:1244–1256`, the multi-combine path checks `native_moe_fuse_hits()`. When true, it skips the standalone `moe_hit_add(...)` and invokes `native_moe_combine_multi_hits(...)`; when false it preserves the old two-stage sequence. `src/kernels/xe/native_moe.cpp:59–109` defaults `STRATA_FUSE_HITS` on, but this branch is still gated by `dec_batch && n > 1 && native_moe_combine_enabled()`. `--native-moe-combine` is opt-in and defaults off (`src/program/generate.cpp:258,586,2068`; the option is also off in curated 17879 at `:249,563,2255`). The existing curated verifier still performs `moe_hit_add` then `native_moe_combine_multi` (`src/core/verify.cpp:1150–1154`), and its native_moe source has no fused hit variant. Thus this is a distinct, not-yet-imported b9 behavior.

The potential work saved is bounded: one kernel launch per grouped verifier-combine call, plus the separate read/modify/write of cache-hit expert partial rows. For each listed hit row the intermediate is a 2,560-float row (10,240 B); a naive source-level upper bound for avoiding its separate read and write is about `2 × hit_rows × 10,240 B`. Actual device-memory traffic depends on cache behavior and is unmeasured. The fused code constructs a per-token hit mask, reads hit rows directly, and computes `(part + hit) * route_weight` in the same order stated by its source comment (`native_moe.cpp:75–106`). This is source-level potential only: floating contraction, mask/pointer validity, and output parity still need executable qualification.

Applicability: it targets the GPU combine on the Xe/SYCL backend and is independent of IQ3_S CPU row math, so it could affect verifier windows for this model on B570 if the engine uses native multi-token combine and cache hits. It cannot reduce one-token decode, and there is no benefit if native combine is off or `n == 1`. Main's supplied active-run status is no MTP / batch zero; that makes this candidate ineligible for that current route unless actual arguments later prove a different multi-token window. No live receipt was opened to infer more.

Required tests before considering a port: compare the old two-kernel and fused paths over deterministic random tensors with `K=10`, every hit count/mask including first/last expert, repeated destinations, zero hits, shared-expert output, multiple tokens, and output-boundary rows; validate pointers/count bounds, asynchronous stream ordering and error propagation; check finite outputs and max/RMS/bitwise error. Then run a bounded device-only kernel timing with the same shapes/hit distributions on B570, and only if that wins, paired end-to-end multi-token decode against the curated source with identical MTP/batch window, cache/profile and route. Preserve single-token behavior and exact greedy/output-quality controls. Existing `native_multi_parity` covers multi-combine without hit folding (`src/kernels/native_multi_parity.cpp`); it does not establish fused-hit correctness.

## B9 CPU/layout deltas that do not qualify for this Qwen route

- B9 adds generic AVX2 multi-token kernels for K-quant formats 10–14 (Q2_K through Q6_K), plus Q8_0 helpers in `src/kernels/cpu/iq_avx2_rows.inl:149–415,507–584` and dispatch wrappers in `iq_avx2.cpp:530+`. `native_expert.cpp:153–188,229–270` selects them for matching types; Q8_0 is restricted to AVX-VNNI. These are new decode support for other packed formats, not a new IQ3_S (21) / IQ4_NL (20) optimization. Do not generalize the source's K-quant measurements (Ryzen 7 5700X) to this Qwen expert pair or to a 5600X.
- B9 generalizes native expert metadata to allow gate and up tensors with separate types/row widths (`native_expert.cpp:61–106`; layout and parser changes in `expert_layout.cpp` and `expert_source.cpp`). That adjusts offsets and runs the two parts separately only when `native_mixed_gu(f)` is true (`native_expert.cpp:190–202`). The stated Qwen IQ3_S gate/up pair has the same format, so this branch is not selected. It may help other mixed-format packs; it is not a speed optimization on this same-type route.
- The one-token AVX2 IQ dispatch remains the same for supported IQ3_S: b9 `native_expert.cpp:130–150` returns threshold one on AVX2/no AVX-512 with the override unset, and IQ3_S is an `iq256_supported` type; the equivalent current curated path is `native_expert.cpp:94–112`. The changed check from `gu_type != 16` to `iq256_supported(gu_type) && gu_type != 16` narrows unsupported formats without changing IQ3_S. Both retain 2,048-byte prefetch (`iq_avx2.cpp:183–200`) and the scalar-versus-gather IQ3_S decoder (`:265–279,299–317,462–470`). Default gather requires Intel hybrid AVX-VNNI/P-core signals (`expert_layout.cpp:111–139`), so it is not the Ryzen automatic path. This repeats R263's gather candidate mechanism and is not new b9 work.
- R263's paired IQ3_S GU-row proposal is already implemented in curated 17879 as an opt-in exact-geometry path (`src/kernels/cpu/iq_avx2.cpp:477–487,517–525`, `STRATA_IQ256_PAIRED_GU`). It is not in b9 and is not a new port candidate; keep its correctness/performance status separate from this b9 comparison. R263's IQ4_NL NT1 possibility also predates b9; b9 does not change its `native_down_rows` dispatch for type 20 (`native_expert.cpp:248–257`).

## Window handoff change and scope

B9's `Verifier::rows/accept_rows` and `InProcessStage::rows` abstraction forwards exactly a `(row0,n)` slice and returns without copying when next-stage input is the same pointer (`src/core/verify.cpp:2683–2687,2744–2753`). Its normal multi-GPU/stage transfer still copies the selected rows when buffers differ. This is a staging/layer-split optimization boundary, not CPU expert arithmetic. Curated 17879 retains pointer-equality guarded handoff copies and has its own partial-row handling; no evidence supports a gain on the supplied single-device route. Do not import the larger stage/pipeline change just to chase a one-device IQ3_S decode target.

## Decision and limitations

For the current one-token decode route, there is no newly discovered b9 CPU-kernel candidate that is both applicable to Qwen IQ3_S/IQ4_NL and absent from curated 17879. The sole ranked b9 opportunity is conditional multi-token GPU hit/combine fusion, which needs batching/MTP, a hit-bearing workload, native combine opt-in, a fused-kernel parity test, and a B570 measurement before it has a place in the recipe. This audit makes no performance claim and recommends no default change.
